info.name: Business Messaging API
info.description:
NestJS backend — PostgreSQL (Neon) + Socket.IO.

**Start:** select the *Business Messaging – Local* environment, run **0. Health & Auth** (stores tokens), then any folder. **2. Full workflow** runs the whole enquiry → delivery flow in order.

Demo password for every user: `demo123`.

request.description: Signs in as {{adminEmail}} and stores the token in `adminToken`.
Signs in as {{agentEmail}} and stores the token in `token`.
Signs in as {{resellerEmail}} and stores the token in `resellerToken`.

item.name: 1. App state & commands
item.description: What the web and mobile apps use.

exec: pm.test("reseller scope, no internal data", () => { const j = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(j.state.scope).to.eql("reseller"); pm.expect(j.state).to.not.have.property("db"); });

item.name: 2. Full workflow (run in order)
item.description: Enquiry → request → reseller accepts & quotes → quote sent → customer approval → order → fulfilment → delivery → completed. Run 0. Health & Auth first.

request.description: Choose a file (PDF, image, txt, csv, docx, xlsx, mp4 — max 10 MB) in the Body tab, then send. Use the returned id in `attachments: [id]`.
Wipes the database and restores the demo data. Run 0. Health & Auth again afterwards.

item.name: 15. Customers (sign-up, login, verification)
item.description: Customer self-registration (email first → password or sign-up), what a customer may reach, and manual verification by our team. Run folder 0 first (admin and reseller tokens). Run this folder in order.

request.description: Step 1 of the login screen. `exists: false` → the app shows the sign-up form.

exec: // a fresh, unused email for this run

request.description: `exists: true` → the app only asks for the password.
Name: letters and spaces only (any language, e.g. Gujarati).
Password: at least 8 characters.

Creates the account and signs the customer in (token + session cookie). With EMAIL_VERIFICATION=true in backend/.env it answers `{ needsVerification: true }` instead and emails a 6-digit code (in development also returned as `devCode` and printed in the backend log).

exec: pm.test("Signed in, or asked for the email code", () => pm.expect(!!j.accessToken || j.needsVerification === true).to.eql(true));

item.name: Sign in (403 email_unverified while email codes are on)

request.description: Right password, but the email isn't confirmed → 403 with `code: "email_unverified"` (the app shows the code screen).

exec: pm.test("Signed in, or asked to confirm the email", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code === 200 || j.code === "email_unverified").to.eql(true));

request.description: At most one new code a minute (and a few per hour). Same answer for emails without an account.

item.name: Confirm email with the code (only with EMAIL_VERIFICATION=true)

request.description: Use the 6-digit code from the email (or `devCode` / the backend log in development). Signs the customer in (token + session cookie). They can buy on P2P at once; selling waits for manual verification.

exec: pm.test("Confirmed, or nothing to confirm", () => pm.expect([200, 400, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

request.description: The app then switches to the password step.

exec: pm.test("Customer scope, no team data", () => { pm.expect(s.scope).to.eql("customer"); pm.expect(s).to.not.have.property("db"); });

pm.test("Own password, chat, ask for price, P2P and own tasks only", () => pm.expect(a.every((x) => ["me.password", "chat.send", "price.request"].includes(x) || /^(p2p|task|list)\./.test(x))).to.eql(true));

request.description: The Customers page in the team dashboard (newest first).

exec: pm.test("New customer listed, unverified", () => { pm.expect(me).to.be.an("object"); pm.expect(me.verified).to.eql(false); });

item.name: Team: verify customer (can sell on P2P)

request.description: Manual verification by our team. Also available as the action `customer.verify`.

item.name: 16. P2P market
item.description: Ads, orders (stock is held while unpaid), payment, release, rating, cancel and appeals. Run folders 0 and 15 first (reseller and customer tokens), then this folder in order.

request.description: Needed before selling. Shown only to the buyer of an open order.
Online ads, your own ads, your orders with their chats (team: also open appeals).

exec: pm.test("Payment details not public", () => pm.expect(s.merchants.every((m) => m.id === s.meId || !m.payTo)).to.eql(true));

request.description: Optional `proof`: id of a file uploaded with POST /files (12. Files).
Decide one with action `p2p.resolveAppeal { id, outcome: "release" | "cancel", note }` (team only).

item.name: 17. Catalog, customer chat & ask for price
item.description: Team catalogue, reseller proposals with approval, customer chat with our team, and "ask for price". Run folders 0 and 15 first.

request.description: Optional `image`: id of an uploaded picture (12. Files). Empty `price` = customers "ask for price".

item.name: Team: add an 'ask for price' service
Team: approve proposal with customer price

request.description: Reject instead: `{ id, approve: false, note }` — the reseller sees the note.

exec: pm.test("No reseller price", () => pm.expect(s.products.every((p) => !("resellerPrice" in p) && !("resellerId" in p))).to.eql(true));

request.description: Files: upload with POST /files (photo, video, PDF, voice note) and pass `attachments: [fileId]` — text is then optional.
Creates a request in the team's Requests, linked to the customer's chat (the quote reaches them there). Without a product: `{ title, category, quantity, area }`.

item.name: Team: the request is in Requests

exec: pm.test("Linked to the chat", () => pm.expect(r && r.conversationId).to.be.a("string"));

item.name: 18. Reminders for everyone
item.description: Team members create reminders that go to everyone (team, resellers, customers); phones notify at the time. Run folder 0 first.

request.description: `dueAt` = epoch milliseconds. Every user gets it in GET /state → `broadcasts`; the phone app shows a notification at that time.
